sections.title: Saying how long a symptom has lasted
sections.content: To say a symptom has lasted a certain amount of time, put a number and a time word before the verb, with -ja/-je added to the time word: két napja ("for two days"), egy hete ("for a week"). Literally it's "of its two days", but it lands as "for two days now". You already know mióta ("since when") as the question; napja/hete gives you the answer.

items.english: My throat has hurt for two days.
How long have you been sick? – For a week.

sections.content: nap ("day") takes -ja (napja), while hét ("week") takes -e and drops its own accent (hete) — a small irregularity worth just memorizing as a fixed phrase.
